title: Dropping the silent -e before adding an ending

blocks.content: Many words end in a silent e — you write it but don't say it, like in 'make'. When you add an ending, that e sometimes has to go.
When a word ends in a silent e, drop the e before adding an ending that starts with a vowel (-ing, -ed, -able).

steps: The ending -ing starts with a vowel.

blocks.explain: 'ride' ends in silent e and -ing starts with a vowel, so drop the e: riding.
blocks.rule: When a word ends in silent e, drop the e before an ending that starts with a vowel.

blocks.content: But KEEP the silent e when the ending starts with a consonant, like -ful or -ly.

blocks.question: Which spelling is correct?
blocks.explain: -ful starts with a consonant, so keep the silent e: hopeful.
blocks.rule: Keep the silent e when the ending starts with a consonant, like -ful or -ly.

blocks.content: Remember: a vowel ending pushes the e out; a consonant ending lets it stay. Let's practise!
